look_here_first: Count leaflets first: fragrant sumac has exactly 3. The leaflets are often fan-shaped, lobed or coarsely toothed on a low suckering deciduous shrub.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: low winter-deciduous clump-forming or suckering shrub

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaflets often fan-shaped, lobed or coarsely toothed

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: compact yellowish flowers appear before or with new leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: female plants produce dark-red hairy drupes

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Ovate to obovate/fan-shaped leaflets, often shallowly to deeply lobed and crenate/coarsely toothed.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Compact yellowish catkin-like clusters before or with leaf-out.

key_traits.label: Safety comparison
key_traits.text: The Anacardiaceae audit explicitly warns against 'leaves of three = poison ivy.' Use habit, leaflet shape/petiolules and fruit architecture; do not test by sap contact.
